primary_source.author: Frederic Pham
primary_source.title: La descente des cols par les onglets de Lefschetz, avec vues sur Gauss-Manin
primary_source.reading_coverage: PartI opening and Section1 setup (printed11-12); PartII finite-critical family setup and Section1.1 local truncated Laplace/regular-singular expansion and integrability footnote (printed22-25); Appendix construction and convergence argument (printed41-44). These selected sections, not the whole manuscript, were read.
primary_source.supported_boundary: Local isolated-critical Laplace periods have power-log asymptotics with positive decay exponents; semialgebraic rapid-decay chains have fixed-phase convergence. The new algebraic profile theorem does not require an unproved global analytic transfer from these facts.
primary_source.not_supplied: A uniform-in-t global sectorial decomposition for the Gaussian nodal degeneration, polynomial tail bounds jointly in t and cut length, or a center-line weighted-period theorem.

literature_search_boundary: Targeted searches for Newton/subdiagram deformations, nodal Gaussian moments and Hardt triviality returned the retained Douai-Sabbah/Long/Wilson sources and Hardt metadata/secondary statements. No new general deformation theorem or Hardt theorem is imported; no full Hardt article read, exhaustive bibliographic sweep or priority claim.
new_exact_argument: After full affine normalization and retention of the metric and means, the Gaussian-perturbed phase has seven finite critical points for every t!=0 by the simple projective infinity node and Bezout. Four normal-form profiles have finite Milnor sums6,4,3,2 and escaping branch counts1,3,4,5. Exact rescaling and the implicit function theorem give all branch actions and Morse Hessians. Their counts exhaust seven. On h=e=f=0 all phase-critical points stay bounded and their axis limits obey (m*T+l_T)*(T^2-4bc)=0.
compact_width: Exact Gaussian completion gives Phi_ss->1/m on compact u in C* and bounded s. This rules out the old width-t model on that compact chart only; u endpoints and s=t*h remain outside the estimate.
critical_action_normalization: For the fractional profiles the full action is k*t plus a nonzero t^(2/n) term. The common k*t must be removed before the scaled limit. Opposite fourth roots can have equal leading actions; no distinct-critical-value hypothesis is inferred.
proof_boundary: The universal Bezout count, conservation of finite Milnor multiplicities, exhaustiveness from degree seven, and the center-line boundedness/limit argument remain written proofs. Symbolic identities and a single exact gradient quotient are not their formal verification.
analytic_boundary: No new GMC class excluded. Counts, Puiseux actions and local Morse Hessians do not by themselves prove a uniform sectorial decomposition or eliminate a constant period. The center-line Gaussian-weighted analysis remains open.
next_gate: Prove a uniform sectorial splitting of the finite Milnor and listed escape Morse blocks, with polynomial tail bounds jointly in t and cut length; separately control the Gaussian-weighted center line and transverse-Hessian degeneracies. Algebraic rank accounting and fixed-t convergence alone do not close this gate.
